title: Notary-Witnessed Hiring Against Deepfake Candidates
one_liner: On-demand licensed notaries sit beside a remote candidate for the final interview or day-one onboarding and sign an attestation.
customer: Security and talent leads at remote-first software, fintech and defence-contractor employers, plus technical recruiting agencies, staffing firms and employer-of-record providers.
problem: An August 2026 eleven-nation advisory warned that North Korean IT-worker operations use real-time deepfakes to beat hiring checks, with 6,500+ similar cases reported globally. Employers face sanctions exposure. Liveness and document checks are being defeated, and the only alternatives are flying candidates in or trusting software.
solution: A marketplace and quality layer over existing mobile notaries and I-9 authorised representatives. A candidate books a witnessed final round in their own city. The witness checks ID, sweeps the room and desk for second screens and earpieces, positions a second camera, and signs a sealed attestation. An optional witnessed live-coding session runs on a locked, company-supplied laptop. A second 10-minute witnessed check at day 30 confirms identity continuity. Coverage starts in 200 US metros and expands to the UK and EU.
why_now: Real-time deepfake interviews are now mainstream and the 11-nation advisory (Aug 2026) is prompting boards to act. The DHS remote I-9 alternative procedure already blesses human 'authorised representatives'. Mobile signing agents lost volume when mortgage origination slumped, so witness supply is cheap.
revenue_model: $150-350 per witnessed session (about 60% to the witness), $2-10k per month enterprise subscriptions, and a per-hire fee for staffing agencies.
non_obvious_insight: Insiders think software has to beat deepfakes. For high-stakes moments, the cheapest defence is physics. A $200 human in the room costs less than one failed hire, and the scarce input is legally recognised people who already verify identity for a living. There are millions of commissioned US notaries.
first_30_days: Sign 40 notaries and loan-signing agents in five metros through signing-agent communities. Write a witness protocol and kit checklist, with legal review of what a notary may attest outside a notarial act. Pilot with three staffing firms or security-conscious startups.

title: Laid-Off Managers Buy Retiring Owners' Funeral Homes
angle: Pairing 1: AI labor-market disruption x Death, estates and the great wealth transfer
one_liner: A matchmaker, training cohort and SBA-loan packager that pairs displaced mid-career operators with retiring owners of independent funeral homes, so local homes stay local and the buyers get AI-proof, trust-based work.
customer: Buyers: laid-off director- and VP-level ops, HR, finance and customer-experience people aged 38-55 with severance, savings or a 401(k) rollover for a down payment. Sellers: independent funeral-home owners aged 60+ with no child taking over (NFDA counts 15,401 US funeral homes, about 75% family or privately owned).
problem: Owners have no succession plan, and their realistic exit is a consolidator (SCI, Everstory and others) that dissolves the local name and pushes preneed. White-collar workers hit by the hiring freeze (Amazon cut about 16,000 corporate roles in Jan 2026; information-sector jobs fell 23K in Aug) cannot find durable human-presence work. Licensing rules and deal mechanics make the path opaque.
solution: A 10-week 'Director-Owner Program': state-by-state licensing roadmap (many states let an unlicensed owner run a home if a licensed director-in-charge is employed, but verify each state), a 6-12 month paid apprenticeship placement inside a partner home before closing, FTC Funeral Rule and preneed-trust training, and SBA 7(a) plus seller-note structuring. Add confidential seller listings and matching. After closing, a shared ops kit (software, price-list compliance, vendor rates) and a peer board of owner-operators.
why_now: SCI's Q2'26 results (preneed sales +7%, operating cash flow +43%, volume -1.4%) show value is in pricing and preneed, not volume, so well-run independents are valuable. Cremation is heading to about 82% by 2045, which lowers facility needs. Consumer interest in green options (61.4%) gives new owners a differentiator that legacy owners ignore. Displaced managers are abundant now.
revenue_model: Buyer tuition of about $4,500 (partly deferred to close). Seller-side success fee of 1.5-3% or $15-25K. Deal-packaging fee of about $5K. Owner-community subscription of $199/mo. Later: software and preneed-admin services.
non_obvious_insight: The funeral-home succession gap and the mid-career white-collar glut are the same problem seen from two ends. The best buyer is a people-good operator, not a financier, and consolidators structurally cannot serve either side: they overpay for scale and cannot preserve local identity. It is the ultimate trust job, and AI cannot hold a widow's hand.
first_30_days: Choose two states with friendly licensing and many rural homes. Phone 100 owners aged 60+ via the state funeral-directors association, aiming for 5 signed no-cost 12-month 'successor search' agreements. Recruit the first 10 buyers from laid-off-manager communities (ex-Amazon alumni groups, LinkedIn, Blind) with a $500 refundable screening deposit. Pre-qualify with one SBA lender. Start 1-2 apprenticeships at partner homes.

title: Visitor-Levy Back Office for Councils
one_liner: White-label registration, returns, audit and enforcement software plus a service desk that lets local councils run a new tourist levy without building it.
customer: Local authorities that have just gained the power to levy visitors: Scottish councils, Welsh councils, and Spanish, Balearic and other European municipalities.
problem: Levies are proliferating (Edinburgh in 2026, Glasgow from Jan 2027, Welsh councils from 2027, Balearics and Catalonia rising, Chicago at 19% hotel tax). Each council must register providers, collect returns, audit and chase non-payers, and most have neither software nor staff. Small B&Bs and self-caterers file badly and disputes pile up.
solution: A packaged portal for provider registration and returns, with support for per-night and percentage levies, exemptions, OTA-collected amounts and platform data feeds. It includes automated reminders, audit sampling, a provider help desk and a statutory report pack, configured per council within weeks.
why_now: New statutory levies start across the UK through 2026-27, and EU short-term rental rules require platforms to share host data with authorities from May 2026. That data can be matched against levy returns. Councils' levy revenue lets them fund administration.
revenue_model: GBP 20-60K per council per year, or a share of collected levy, plus per-return service fees for the help desk.
non_obvious_insight: Levies fail on administration rather than on rate-setting. Every council needs the same back office at the same moment, and levy revenue pays for it, so the customer has a budget line before it has a system.
first_30_days: Talk to 10 councils and the Welsh and Scottish local-government bodies. Offer a fixed-fee pilot of a provider portal and returns form for one small council. Build it from a form tool and a database first, then harden.

title: Waste-Fat Origin Passports for 45Z Fuel
one_liner: Collector-level audits, chain of custody and lab fingerprinting that prove a load of used cooking oil or animal fat is North American.
customer: Renewable diesel, SAF and biodiesel producers, feedstock traders, and UCO collectors who want a price premium for proven origin.
problem: Since 2026, the 45Z clean-fuel credit has been limited to North American feedstocks, which creates an incentive to relabel imported UCO as domestic. Existing testing labs certify samples, not the collection chain, and producers face audit and credit-clawback risk.
solution: An 'origin passport' per load: KYC and site audits of collectors, GPS-tagged pickups, retained samples, and lab fingerprinting (fatty-acid and sterol profile, stable isotopes) against a growing reference library, delivered as per-load certificates and a traceability dashboard.
why_now: The 45Z origin restriction took effect for fuel made after 2025, so proof of origin has become a price factor. A UCO import surge and past fraud scandals mean auditors will look hard.
revenue_model: Per-load certificate fee of a few cents per gallon, annual collector audit fee, and subscription for producers.
non_obvious_insight: Waste is a fraud-prone commodity because the seller controls the paperwork. Verifying the collection chain, not the oil, is where enforcement will go.
first_30_days: Sign 2-3 mid-size collectors and one independent biodiesel producer as design partners. Build a reference sample library from those partners. Set up a lab partnership. Run first 20 loads with passports.

title: Payment-Slip Doctor for Foreign Residents
one_liner: A LINE service that lets a foreign resident photograph a Japanese payment slip or government letter and get a plain explanation, deadline, consequences and payment help in their own language.
customer: Japanese-language schools, vocational schools and universities with many foreign students, at about ¥300 per student per month. Later customers are municipal national-health-insurance departments paying for improved collection, employers of foreign staff, and rent-guarantee and property-management firms.
problem: Foreign residents paid on average only 63% of national health insurance premiums by the end of 2024, according to a survey of about 150 local governments. From around FY2027, unpaid premiums and pension contributions will be a ground to deny visa renewal or change of status. Yet at my counter, foreign customers regularly hand me a slip or official letter and ask what it means. The barcode on a konbini payment slip is void after the due date, so I have to refuse it. Then a worker who cannot get to the ward office in daytime faces an arrears spiral that may end in a denied visa. The government mails a notice in Japanese that looks like junk mail.
solution: Photograph the slip or letter. The service reads the barcode and text, identifies the document type such as national health insurance, resident tax, pension or traffic fine, and explains in Vietnamese, Nepali, Chinese, Burmese or Indonesian what it is, how much, when due, and the consequences of non-payment. It sets calendar reminders and links to pay by PayPay, bank app or konbini. If the slip is expired, it generates a reissue script and shows ward-office hours and the nearest late-opening branch. Anything ambiguous or legal is escalated to a partner administrative scrivener. Stickers with a QR code at konbini payment counters are the acquisition channel.
why_now: The 2026 system upgrades that will link municipal payment records to Immigration Services Agency data, plus the rule that unpaid premiums will block renewals from around 2027, make payment compliance a visa issue for hundreds of thousands of students and workers. The current government has made foreign-resident rule enforcement a political priority. Schools are already adding payment-tracking features to their student systems. Nobody has built the explanation layer, and translation apps do not decode payment slips or their deadlines.
revenue_model: Schools pay ¥300-500 per student per month. Municipalities pay per successful on-time payment or a share of recovered arrears. Employers pay per foreign employee per month. Property managers and guarantors pay per tenant. A small paid human-escalation tier costs the user ¥980 per case.
non_obvious_insight: The failure point is not language in general. It is a single document, the konbini payment slip, and a single hidden rule that its barcode dies on the due date. People miss it by a day and the consequence is a visa problem. The counter clerk sees this daily, so the demand is proven and concentrated. Because the buyer of the outcome is a school or municipality, the paying customer is not the end user.
first_30_days: Build the LINE OA with barcode decoding, OCR and slip-type rules for the five most common slips, and Vietnamese, Nepali and Chinese output reviewed by native speakers. Put QR stickers on the payment counters of my three stores. Pilot with two Osaka language schools, about 300 students, at ¥300 per student per month. Measure on-time payment before and after. Bring the results to one ward's national health insurance department. Partner with an administrative scrivener firm for the escalation tier.

title: Tip Passport: Mortgage-Ready Records for Tipped Workers
one_liner: An app that logs every cash and card tip in a lender-grade ledger so young bartenders, stylists, servers and valets can claim the new tip deduction and finally qualify for a mortgage or lease.
customer: Gen Z and young-millennial tipped workers (servers, bartenders, hair and nail techs, barbers, delivery and other occupations on the IRS list) earning $50-$120k with largely undocumented cash tips. Lenders and landlords pay for verified income.
problem: Cash tips have long been under-reported to avoid tax, so returns show low income and lenders qualify people on returns and W-2s. A stylist netting $90k cannot get a mortgage. The new deduction of up to $25,000 in qualified tips makes reporting valuable, but workers have no system, fear audits, and employer POS captures only card tips.
solution: One-tap, voice and QR tip logging with imports from Venmo, Cash App and POS. It produces monthly tip statements in IRS-recognized format, a deduction-ready schedule, a tax-reserve estimate and a 'lender pack' with 24-month income narrative reconciled to bank deposits. The pack is accepted by partner bank-statement lenders and landlords. Built-in classification excludes service charges and mandatory gratuities that do not qualify.
why_now: Final regulations (TD 10044) published April 13, 2026 confirm the 70+ qualifying occupations for the deduction on tips received in 2025-2028. 2026 is the first year workers can plan around it. The sunset after 2028 creates a roughly two-year window to build the 24-month record lenders want, and non-QM bank-statement lending is available.
revenue_model: $8-$12 per month or $79 per year, a lender referral fee of $300-$1,500 per funded loan, $25 per landlord verification report, and a B2B retention perk sold to salon suites and restaurant groups.
non_obvious_insight: A tax incentive flips the incentive from hiding income to documenting it for the first time in decades, and the same document (proof of income) is worth ten times the tax savings because it unlocks a mortgage. The moat is trusted, lender-accepted record-keeping, not tax prep.
first_30_days: Find 100 stylists and bartenders through salon-suite communities and beauty and hospitality creators on social media. Sell a tip ledger plus deduction estimate at $9 per month. Partner with one bank-statement lender and one CPA who signs off on the statement format. Track pre-approvals within 90 days as the proof point.

title: Dr. Simi USA: Pharmacy-Plus-Consult for the Uninsured
one_liner: Small-format, generic-first pharmacies with a nurse-practitioner consult room beside the counter, posted cash prices and no insurance needed, following Mexico's Farmacias Similares model and landing in US pharmacy deserts.
customer: Uninsured and underinsured adults in pharmacy deserts and immigrant neighborhoods. An estimated 4.8M Americans lost coverage after the enhanced ACA subsidies expired, and about 48M people live in pharmacy deserts. The second customer is at-risk independent pharmacists who license the clinic kit.
problem: Rite Aid is gone (all stores closed after its 2025 Chapter 11), Walgreens is shrinking, and independents are squeezed by PBM reimbursement. An uninsured person with a UTI or sinus infection faces a $150-250 urgent-care visit plus retail drug prices, so many just skip treatment.
solution: An 800-1,200 sq ft store or a 200 sq ft conversion inside an existing independent pharmacy. A flat $25-40 NP consult (loss leader), point-of-care tests (strep, flu, UTI, A1c), on-site dispensing of generics at transparent cost-plus prices, bilingual staff, and chronic-refill programs. The visit and the dispense happen in one 10-minute stop, so there is no abandoned prescription. Mexico's Farmacias Similares runs thousands of outlets with an attached doctor's office charging a few dollars.
why_now: Coverage is shrinking at the same time as pharmacy access: enhanced ACA subsidies lapsed at the end of 2025, Medicaid cuts phase in through 2026-27, and Rite Aid's liquidation left holes in low-income neighborhoods. Cost Plus Drugs has taught Americans to expect transparent generic prices, so a cash-price store is no longer strange.
revenue_model: Dispensing margin on generics, flat consult fees, point-of-care lab fees, OTC sales, plus licensing or franchise fees for the turnkey clinic-in-a-pharmacy kit sold to independents.
non_obvious_insight: Don't compete with telehealth on convenience; win on adjacency. Consult plus dispense in one stop removes the biggest leak in cash-pay care, which is people who get a prescription and never fill it. The fastest route isn't building stores at all. It is converting existing independents on the edge of closure by giving them a second revenue line, and an already-licensed pharmacy removes months of setup.
first_30_days: Recruit 3 independent pharmacies in Latino neighborhoods (Texas, Florida or Illinois). Contract per-diem NPs under a collaborative practice agreement, build a 100 sq ft consult room, and print a simple price list ('$29 visit, $4 generics'). Market through WhatsApp groups, churches and community radio. Run a 60-day pilot and track visit-to-fill conversion and margin per visit.

title: Parametric Recovery Cover for Tourism Towns
angle: Pairing 1: Climate adaptation x Travel/hospitality (insurance retreat and destination dependence)
one_liner: Annual parametric policies bought by destination tourism boards that pay out within days when fire, smoke, flood or road closures crater visitor demand, even with no physical damage.
customer: Destination marketing organizations and county or city tourism authorities in single-access, hazard-exposed resort towns (Estes Park, Truckee/Tahoe, Big Bear, Gatlinburg, Outer Banks, Asheville, Maui), funded by lodging taxes (transient occupancy tax, TOT) with $50-500K premium budgets.
problem: Business-interruption cover requires physical damage, and civil-authority riders are short. After Lahaina, Asheville and Caldor, the losses came from closed roads, smoke and perception, not damaged hotels. TOT revenue funds recovery marketing and services, and it collapses exactly when the town most needs to advertise. Retail insurers are retreating from these towns and small lodging and restaurants cannot buy adequate cover.
solution: We design tourism-specific indices and place the cover. Triggers use hazard evidence (evacuation orders, AQI days over threshold, DOT road-closure days) confirmed by an occupancy drop versus baseline (STR/hotel data such as AirDNA). Payout scales are calibrated to historical TOT dips. The policyholder is the DMO, which re-grants through its existing marketing and small-business grant programs. Capacity comes from a fronting carrier or parametric MGA plus reinsurers and ILS. We deliver index design, backtests, placement and the claims data oracle.
why_now: Reinsurance is softening fast: Howden reports property-cat risk-adjusted rates down up to 25% at 1 June 2026 after -16% and -14.7% earlier, with record capital (about $790B, secondary source). Niche capacity is now cheap while retail carriers still retreat. Cat bond issuance hit records in H1 2026 (about $18B). Travel booking windows are about 33 days, so a fast cash-funded comeback campaign can restore bookings quickly.
revenue_model: Broker/MGA-style commission of 12-18% of premium, plus index licensing and annual re-modeling fees. Ten towns at about $150K average premium and 15% commission is roughly $225K in year one, scaling through state travel associations.
non_obvious_insight: Tourism loss after disasters is mostly access and perception, not damage. A public tourism board is the rare buyer that can purchase parametric cover and redistribute it to small businesses that could never qualify individually. The lodging-tax series is a clean, public, monthly loss history no adjuster touched. Public-entity buyers also sidestep the homeowner rate-filing regime that strangles retail products.
first_30_days: Backtest four past events (East Troublesome/Estes Park 2020, Caldor/Tahoe 2021, Lahaina 2023, Helene/Asheville 2024) using public TOT reports, AQI and road-closure logs. Produce 'what you would have received' one-pagers. Pitch 10 DMO executive directors and 3 state travel associations. Get a parametric MGA or fronting partner to quote. Target the first bound policy in the spring 2027 budget and fire-season renewal window.

title: Coder-Signed Reasonable-Value Reports for Injury Defense
one_liner: A 48-hour, coder-certified benchmark report that tells defense lawyers and auto carriers what a letter-of-protection medical bill is actually worth.
customer: Insurance defense law firms and auto-carrier litigation/SIU units handling bodily-injury claims in tort-reform states (Florida, Georgia, Texas, Louisiana first). Volume firms pay per report. Carriers pay monthly.
problem: Plaintiff-side injury cases increasingly rest on treatment provided under letters of protection (LOP), where the provider is paid from the settlement and bills at a private rate card. Defense lawyers have to show what the care is really worth. Today that means a $3-5k billing expert, a slow turnaround, and a fight over methodology. Most claims examiners cannot read a CMS-1500 or UB-04, so inflated bills mostly get paid or settled at face value.
solution: Intake the itemized bill and records. Map every line to CPT/HCPCS and revenue codes and flag unbundling (e.g. 99215-25 plus separate injection administration, physician-owned ASC facility fees stacked on the professional fee, stacked imaging reads). Benchmark each line against Medicare multiples, hospital-posted commercial negotiated rates from price-transparency files, and local percentiles. The output is a Daubert-hardened PDF signed by a certified coder (CPC/CCS) with an optional expert declaration or testimony upsell. It is a methodology plus a template, so the marginal cost per report is about an hour of coder time.
why_now: Florida's 2023 tort reform made LOP arrangements discoverable and admitted evidence of amounts actually paid. Georgia's 2025 tort reform pushed similar rules, and other states are copying. Hospital price-transparency rules that took full effect in 2026 now require actual payment amounts where rates are percentages or algorithms, so a defensible local benchmark exists for the first time.
revenue_model: $295-$695 per report. Expert declaration or testimony at $1,500-$3,500. $2-5k/month subscriptions for carriers and volume firms with a report quota. Gross margin is high because coders are paid per report as contractors.
non_obvious_insight: Inside a hospital, chargemaster prices are understood to be fiction, and every biller knows what things really get paid. Injury lawyers have been arguing about 'reasonable value' without that insider map. Certified coders also know the tells of bills built for litigation rather than payment: modifier-25 patterns, unbundled facility fees, and E/M levels that no insurer would ever pay. The market is starved of people credentialed and willing to say so on paper. The moat is a coder bench plus a methodology that survives cross-examination, not software.
first_30_days: Recruit 3-5 CPC/CCS coders (ex-hospital, remote, contractors) and one defense-attorney advisor to review the methodology memo. Build the report template from the free Medicare fee schedules plus a few metro-area price-transparency files. Cold-email about 100 Florida and Georgia defense firms and claims managers, and offer 5 free reports on live cases in exchange for a methodology review and a testimonial. Convert the first 3-5 to $349 per report, then price the expert declaration as an add-on.

title: Rent Seasonal Nitrate Treatment, Don't Build Plants
one_liner: Trailer-mounted nitrate-removal skids rented to small farm-belt utilities only for the 60-120 days a year when river or shallow-well nitrate spikes.
customer: Small and mid-size utilities (500-10,000 people) in Iowa, Nebraska, Illinois, Minnesota, Kansas and Wisconsin that draw from rivers or shallow aquifers. Systems with recent nitrate MCL violations are first. The utility pays, and state programs may help.
problem: More than 60M Americans are served from elevated-nitrate sources, and the 10 ppm limit dates from 1991. EPA's cancer review has stalled since 2023, and its research office is gone. Small rural systems bear treatment costs alone. A permanent $2-10M plant is out of reach for them, though the exceedance is seasonal.
solution: A fleet of containerized nitrate-selective ion-exchange skids sized 0.25-2 MGD. Include resin regeneration, brine logistics (the make-or-break piece, so pre-agree the disposal route with the wastewater plant or a hauler), operator training and remote monitoring. Priced as a seasonal service, per 1,000 gallons treated with a seasonal minimum. Start asset-light by leasing skids from an existing ion-exchange OEM.
why_now: Federal action on nitrate is stalled, so relief is not coming from Washington. Broad drought followed by heavy runoff swings nitrate hard. The FY2026 $7.2B SRF pool makes states receptive to flexible compliance solutions. The 10 ppm limit is still enforceable today.
revenue_model: Seasonal rental of $15-40k/month per skid plus per-gallon regeneration and brine fees, under 3-5 year master service agreements.
non_obvious_insight: Insiders assume compliance means permanent capital. But nitrate is a peak problem (Des Moines Water Works runs its removal plant only during high-nitrate stretches, from my background knowledge), so the winning model sells the peak, not the plant. A rental converts an unfundable capital project into a fundable operating line.
first_30_days: Pull three years of nitrate MCL violations from the public SDWIS database and build a list of 100 systems. Call five directly and through a state rural water association. Sign an MOU with one ion-exchange OEM for lease-back skids, and get one utility to agree to a paid pilot for spring 2027.

title: Contingency-Fee Audit of OTA Markups and Payouts
one_liner: Mystery-shop every downstream reseller and reconcile every OTA payout, then take a share of the money and direct bookings recovered.
customer: Independent hotels of 20-200 rooms and small groups in Europe and the US paying 15-28% commissions.
problem: 51% of European hotels say OTAs sell below their loaded rate, up from 40% two years ago, and 26% do not know whether rates are passed on. Markups by Agoda, Citi, AA, Southwest and loyalty partners are invisible to rate-shopping tools. Hotels are paid after checkout, and commission, virtual-card fee and no-show errors go unchecked. In-house monitoring exists for chains (Radisson watches 1,600 properties), but independents have nothing.
solution: Combine automated and human shoppers that check rates across OTAs and reseller portals with screenshots per date, and reservation-level reconciliation of booked rate, commission, payout, card fees, cancellations and no-shows. Produce evidence packs to send to OTA account managers and a price-integrity dashboard that supports the case for direct booking.
why_now: Booking's payment service touched about 70% of its 2025 bookings, which concentrates the opacity. Google AI Overviews now reportedly show hotel prices and cut metasearch clicks, which pushes hotels to defend direct channels. Channel managers now expose reservation data.
revenue_model: 20-25% of recovered commission and no-show revenue, plus USD 99-299 per month for ongoing price-integrity monitoring.
non_obvious_insight: OTAs cannot audit themselves and hotels cannot see downstream markups, the same structural gap that made freight-bill and telecom-audit firms lucrative. The shopping evidence is the leverage in negotiations.
first_30_days: Offer 20 hotels a free 'leak report' covering 30 future dates, using human plus scripted shoppers. Convert the worst-leaking ones to contingency contracts, using hotel associations for introductions.

title: Zero-Commission Motor Third-Party Renewal Rails
one_liner: If motor third-party pays agents 0%, nobody sells the mandatory cover, so insurers need a cost-plus renewal utility.
customer: Indian general insurers, especially public-sector ones, and fleet owners; insurers pay a per-renewal fee.
problem: The IRDAI draft (Sep 23) cuts commission caps from 30% to 20%, sets 0% on motor third-party and 5% on own-damage. PB Fintech fell 36% in a day, and agents and aggregators lose any reason to chase mandatory renewals.
solution: Automated renewal reminders using expiry data from dealers and registration records, sent as WhatsApp messages in local languages with UPI payment. Charge a flat servicing fee. The wedge is two-wheeler third-party renewals in one state for one insurer.
why_now: The draft is out for comment now, and insurers must find distribution that costs less than commission.
revenue_model: Rs 30-80 per renewal from the insurer, with own-damage upsell.
non_obvious_insight: When distribution stops paying, a mandatory product needs a utility rather than a marketplace, and the underwriter is the natural buyer. The draft could change, so build for both outcomes.
first_30_days: Pitch three insurers. Run a 5,000-vehicle renewal test using expiry lists from a dealer network.

title: Federated Settlement-Benchmark Co-op for Small Firms
one_liner: Small plaintiff firms pool de-identified settlement outcomes from their practice-management systems to get case-value benchmarks that only insurers and big firms have today.
customer: Employment, wage-hour, personal-injury, med-mal and consumer boutiques with 1-15 attorneys. Later buyers are insurers, litigation funders and mediators purchasing aggregate indices.
problem: Verdict reporters capture only the few percent of cases that reach verdict, while nearly all money moves through confidential settlements. Insurers hold large claims databases, but plaintiff-side lawyers estimate value from gut feel and listservs. Frontier legal tools train on public opinions, not private outcomes, and outcome-priced legal work (as Norm Law sells) needs outcome data.
solution: With attorney approval, a practice-management connector extracts a handful of structured fields (claim type, venue, injury or violation class, damages band, procedural posture, time to resolution, fee outcome) into a secure aggregation layer with k-anonymity thresholds and differential privacy on outputs, no free text, and respect for confidentiality clauses. Members get instant valuation ranges and time-to-resolution, and aggregate indices are licensed to insurers and funders.
why_now: MCP connectors to practice-management systems are now real (8am: 60+ small firms in month one), privacy-preserving analytics tooling has matured, and outcome-based pricing plus a funded litigation-finance market create demand for outcome data.
revenue_model: Free for contributors (about 5 data points per quarter), $99-299/month for non-contributors, and $25-250k/year data licenses to insurers and funders.
non_obvious_insight: The most valuable legal dataset is in no court file. It sits in hundreds of thousands of small-firm ledgers. Firms will trade aggregated outcomes for benchmarks (as doctors do for registries), and Westlaw cannot copy that give-to-get flywheel because it has no view into settlements. Rule 1.6 and settlement confidentiality clauses are the main risk and need an ethics memo up front.
first_30_days: Run it manually first. Recruit 20 employment or wage-hour lawyers through a state bar section or NELA chapter, collect 10 de-identified data points each on a form, return a valuation sheet, and commission an ethics counsel memo. Then build the connector for one platform.

title: Pay-on-Pass: Inspections Trigger Sub Payments
one_liner: Same-day payment to framers and foundation crews the moment the city inspection clears, financed against the builder's draw.
customer: Small private builders (20-300 homes a year) and their framing, foundation, plumbing and electrical subs, with a community lender or credit line as funding partner.
problem: Cities adopt AI plan review, filings surge (Honolulu applications +34% but permits issued +5%, backlog 9,252), and the bottleneck moves to post-permit inspections. Subs wait for the pass, then wait for payment: one in five subs waits 60+ days and GCs are 4x more likely than subs to be paid within 30 days. Crews are already vanishing, so slow payers lose them.
solution: A payment rail keyed to a third-party-verified milestone: inspection status pulled from municipal portals or a photo of the green tag. The sub is paid within 24 hours from a revolving credit facility, repaid from the builder's draw within 30 days. Builders also get a crew reliability ranking and inspection-queue analytics by jurisdiction and inspector, with photo pre-checks to raise first-time pass rates.
why_now: AI permitting is deploying now (Honolulu, Denver's $4.6M contract), shifting the constraint downstream. Immigration enforcement makes verified crews scarce, so pay speed has become a recruiting tool. Completions are down 27.1%.
revenue_model: 1.5-2.5% of released payments, paid by the builder for speed and crew retention, with an optional sub-paid instant-pay discount. Spread on credit line usage.
non_obvious_insight: The inspection pass is the only moment in construction that is third-party verified, timestamped and dispute-proof, which makes it the ideal payment trigger and collateral. Nobody uses it because the data sits in thousands of scattered municipal portals, but one builder in one metro needs only three or four.
first_30_days: Pick one metro and its three permit portals. Pilot with 3 builders and their 5 framing and foundation subs. Open a $100-200K line with a friendly community lender. Verify passes by hand and pay by ACH.

title: Cross-Landlord Fake-Employer and Fake-Reference Registry
one_liner: A shared network that spots rental fraud by the out-of-band details forgers cannot fake, such as the same 'HR' phone number, burner line or 'previous landlord' reused across dozens of leasing offices.
customer: Independent and mid-size property managers (50 to 5,000 units) who process applications themselves and lack a fraud team. They pay per application or per portfolio. Later customers are auto lenders, buy-here-pay-here dealers, gig-work platforms and small-balance mortgage lenders, who all verify employers and references the same way.
problem: Application fraud is now professional. The pay stubs, bank statements and offer letters are fabricated, and the 'employer' is a shell whose 'HR line' is answered by an accomplice. Even the 'previous landlord' reference is a friend. Every leasing office catches one of these files, throws it out, and never tells anyone. The same ring then applies at the property across town and eventually gets a lease. The eviction that follows costs $8,000 to $20,000 and several months. Document-forensics tools catch sloppy Photoshop, but once image generators can produce perfect pay stubs (as they now can), the lie is no longer in the PDF. It is in the phone number and the employer that do not exist.
solution: An API and browser extension for leasing staff. Staff enter the employer name, HR phone or email, the previous-landlord contact and the stated address. The system returns a risk read built from three signals. First, telecom line-type and age (VoIP or burner, number recently ported or activated). Second, business-registry and domain checks (EIN, formation date, mismatched address, brand-new domain). Third, and this is the moat, network signals: how many distinct applicants at how many unrelated landlords used this exact phone, email, employer or landlord reference in the last 12 months, and whether any of those files were confirmed fraud by a participating PM. Participants contribute confirmed-fraud entities and get read access, and entries link to entities (phones, domains, businesses), not to named individuals. That design keeps most of the data outside consumer-report regulation, and any person-linked entry gets a dispute and correction workflow.
why_now: Generative image models make forged financial documents indistinguishable in 2025 and 2026, which pushes the defensive signal from document pixels to out-of-band verification. Fraud-detection vendors for leasing are consolidating around documents, so an entity-level shared registry sits in the gap. Large PMs have internal fraud teams, and the long tail of independents has nothing. Rental markets that are softer with more concessions also attract more fraud-ring activity aimed at free-rent giveaways and quick move-ins.
revenue_model: $1.50 to $3.00 per application check, or $149 to $499 per month by portfolio size with a contribution-based discount. Enterprise API licensing to lenders and platforms later. Data-contribution credits make the network self-seeding.
non_obvious_insight: Rental fraud rings reuse infrastructure across landlords far more than they reuse identities. The same 'HR' number answers for 14 different companies. But no single landlord sees more than one or two, so the pattern is invisible without a network. It works like ISO ClaimSearch did for insurance claims. Because the registry tracks entities and not people, it sidesteps most of the fair-lending and consumer-reporting objections that killed earlier landlord blacklists.
first_30_days: Recruit 10 PMs from local NARPM chapters and landlord Facebook groups. Ask each to send the last 20 to 50 confirmed-fraud files (phone, email, employer, reference only, no SSNs), and seed the database from those. Run the pooled data for overlaps and show each PM how many of their 'unique' fraudsters overlapped with someone else's. Ship a Chrome extension that checks a phone or email against the database plus Twilio Lookup. Free for the first 60 days for contributors, then $149 per month. Have a fair-credit-reporting attorney review the entity-only design and the dispute process before charging.

title: Sovereign Data Vaults in Orbit
one_liner: Encrypted national-records backups stored in orbit, out of reach of seizure, cyber-wipe or flood.
customer: Governments of small, exposed or at-risk states (Baltics, Pacific island nations, Ukraine, Taiwan-type buyers), central banks and national archives.
problem: Countries already run 'data embassies' in friendly data centers, but those still sit on someone's soil. A wipe, seizure, war or sea-level loss can strand civil registries, land titles and treasury records.
solution: Start with a hosted-payload vault on a partner satellite: an append-only, radiation-tolerant encrypted store holding registries and legal records, with keys held by the customer under multi-party control and a dead-man retrieval process. Grow into dedicated vault satellites.
why_now: Rideshare pricing makes small payloads cheap. 2025 demonstrations of storage and compute in orbit (Lonestar's data payloads, Starcloud's reported H100 launch) showed the concept works. Geopolitical risk to state data has risen.
revenue_model: Feasibility studies $50-150k. Multi-year vault contracts of $1-5M per year. Per-TB-year storage fees after launch.
non_obvious_insight: Governments already pay for offshore backups. The extraterritorial jurisdiction of orbit can be sold as a legal and physical guarantee, not as a gadget.
first_30_days: Approach digital-government offices in Estonia, Tuvalu, Ukraine and Taiwan-type buyers with a paid feasibility study. Line up a hosted-payload slot with an existing operator. Design the key-custody model with a legal adviser on treaty and jurisdiction questions.

title: Ex-Botter Red Team for Limited Drops
one_liner: Pay former sneaker-bot users to attack your product drop before launch, then rent you the checkout filter that stops what they found.
customer: Indie brands that run limited drops on Shopify with 500 to 5,000 units: streetwear labels, collectible toy and art-toy makers, TCG shops, sneaker boutiques, merch stores, small beauty and food brands. They pay $750 to $2,500 per pentest, then a per-drop or monthly fee.
problem: Brands think a waiting room or Cloudflare stops scalpers. It only stops speed. Real resellers win by multiplying identities, not by being fast. They use Gmail dot and plus tricks and catch-all domains, address jigging (Apt vs Unit vs #, an extra letter in the street name), virtual cards from one issuer, and residential proxies. One 'customer' becomes 40 orders. Fans get nothing, the brand gets angry DMs, and the resale premium goes to strangers. Small brands cannot afford enterprise bot vendors and do not know what to look for.
solution: Wedge: a 'Drop Pentest'. We run a real reseller stack against the brand's store or staging a week before launch and hand back a report: 'we would have captured 38% of your units, here is how'. Product: a Shopify checkout app called One Per Human. It normalizes emails, fuzzy-dedupes addresses (USPS-style standardization plus apartment and unit variants), clusters card fingerprints and BINs, phone-verifies and blocks VoIP numbers, and flags or auto-cancels suspected multiples before fulfillment, with a human review queue. Optional 'verified reseller tier' at a higher price so the brand captures some of the flip premium legitimately.
why_now: Collectible drops have become a public mess in 2025-26: Labubu and other Pop Mart drops, and Pokemon TCG releases where stores had fights, lines, and pulled product. Indie brands now copy sneaker-style drops, with sneaker-style bot pressure. Cheap LLM fuzzy matching makes address and identity dedupe far cheaper to build than it was two years ago. Shopify's checkout extensibility gives apps a place to validate or flag orders.
revenue_model: Pentest at $750 to $2,500. Guard app at $149 to $499 per drop, or 0.5% to 1% of drop GMV. Annual contracts for brands that drop monthly.
non_obvious_insight: Bots do not beat drops on speed. They beat them on identity multiplication, and the tells sit in the order data (address shape, email pattern, card issuer clusters) that the brand already has. Only someone who has run the tricks knows which tells matter. The poacher-turned-gamekeeper credibility is the moat, and the pentest report sells the product by showing the brand its own leak.
first_30_days: Days 1 to 7: build the attack checklist from what I and my Discord friends already do. Days 7 to 14: DM 100 small Shopify brands with an upcoming drop on Instagram, offering a free mini-audit built from their public store, such as how easy it is to create fake variants of an address. Days 14 to 30: convert 3 to 5 into paid pentests at $750 and use the findings to pre-sell the app. Delivery is mostly a spreadsheet plus screenshots.

title: Retraining-Backed Severance for AI Layoffs
one_liner: Employers replace resume-coaching outplacement with prepaid seats in shortage-role training plus a guaranteed interview pipeline, priced per re-employed worker.
customer: HR and people-ops leaders at 500-20,000 person employers doing AI-related restructuring; hiring employers in healthcare and trades pay placement fees.
problem: Employment of 22-25 year-olds in AI-exposed jobs is 19% below trend and recent grads are 42% underemployed. About half the earnings loss comes from landing in restaurants and retail. Traditional outplacement coaches people back toward the same shrinking roles.
solution: Displaced workers choose from vetted 8-16 week programs into shortage jobs (medical assistant, EMT, CDL, electrician pre-apprenticeship, revenue-cycle, dental support). The employer funds tuition and a stipend from severance budget. Hiring partners guarantee interviews. Use Workforce Pell where a program is approved. Success fee at 90-day retention.
why_now: AI-linked layoffs are drawing PR and political pressure. Workforce Pell has only 5 approved programs, so employer-funded pathways are the fast lane. Employers in experience-rated unemployment-insurance states may also gain from faster re-employment (verify by state).
revenue_model: $4-9k per participant paid by the employer, replacing a $3-5k outplacement fee, plus $1-3k placement fees from hiring partners.
non_obvious_insight: Insiders assume laid-off white-collar workers should look for adjacent white-collar roles. Those roles are the ones disappearing. Severance is already budgeted money, so converting a slice into a retraining voucher aimed at shortage roles costs the employer little and buys reputation.
first_30_days: Build 3 vetted pathways with local providers in one metro. Pitch 20 HR heads at companies that recently announced cuts. Run a single 25-person pilot and collect 90-day placement outcomes for references.

title: Human Viva Examiners for AI-Wary Universities
angle: Education, credentialing and skills after AI x Emerging markets leapfrogging
one_liner: A per-student oral-defense service where trained examiners in Nairobi, Manila and Chennai run 12-minute recorded vivas on submitted essays and code, giving US professors human-verified authorship evidence for about $10 a student.
customer: Writing-program directors, department chairs and online-degree program managers at US community colleges and mid-size universities (intro composition, intro CS, gateway business courses). Individual adjuncts with discretionary budgets are the first buyers. Admissions offices reviewing flagged essays come second.
problem: Harvard data from Sept 2026: 89% of professors received suspected AI work, 67% say AI hurts their courses, and only 12% referred cases to the honor council. Detectors are unreliable and biased against non-native writers. Nobody has the time or the standing to test an accusation, and a professor cannot personally hold 60 oral exams per section.
solution: The instructor uploads submissions and a rubric. The platform drafts 4-6 questions specific to each student's own paper. AI writes the questions but never judges. A vetted examiner in a matching time zone runs a 12-minute live video viva, scores it against the rubric, and marks the student as able or unable to explain their own work. The instructor gets a one-page evidence summary and the recording within 48 hours. Examiners are ex-teachers and graduate students who pass a 6-hour certification, and 10% of vivas are double-scored for QA. Students consent through the syllabus, and the institution signs a FERPA school-official agreement.
why_now: Faculty AI distress peaked in Sept 2026. NYC and LAUSD paused classroom AI for 2026-27, so 'human-verified' is now politically favored over AI-judging-AI. Proctored math accuracy has fallen from about 80% to about 60% while unsupervised work looks better. Meanwhile English-fluent graduates in Kenya, the Philippines and India face a shrinking entry-level BPO ladder, so a large trainable labor pool is available at $15/hour.
revenue_model: $9-14 per viva billed to the department, with examiners paid about $4-5 per viva (roughly $15/hour), for a gross margin near 55%. Departments can buy an annual site licence of $3-10k. An appeal viva is a $25 add-on.
non_obvious_insight: The bottleneck is not detection, it is credible human attention. Detectors create accusations nobody can test, while a viva turns an accusation into an assessment: if the student can defend the paper, they learned it, however they drafted it. The only way to supply cheap, trusted, trained human minutes at scale is emerging-market labor, and the only buyers who will pay are institutions that just lost faith in remote work.
first_30_days: Recruit and train 15 examiners through two teacher-training colleges or alumni groups in Kenya and the Philippines. Offer three community-college composition instructors a free 30-student pilot and record what share of students cannot explain their own paper. Charge $300 for the next batch, and reach instructors through adjunct communities and online-program managers. Run it on Zoom, a calendar tool and Airtable, with no custom platform until 10 paying sections exist.

title: Fee-Free Hire Receipts for Migrant Workers
one_liner: A worker-held credential proving a migrant was recruited without fees and paid as contracted, sold to suppliers and brands that must prove no forced labour, and portable to the worker's next job.
customer: Tier-1 suppliers and their EU-facing brand buyers in electronics, garments, construction, hospitality and palm oil. Ethical recruitment agencies are a channel, and the worker is the holder.
problem: From 14 December 2027 the EU Forced Labour Regulation bans products made with forced labour, and importers must prove a negative. Audits are sampled snapshots that are easy to game. Workers in corridors such as Nepal to Malaysia or the Philippines to the Gulf often pay illegal recruitment fees that create debt bondage, and they leave with no portable record of employment or skills.
solution: A WhatsApp-first Hire Receipt. At contract signing the worker gets a signed record of recruiter, employer, wage, contract terms and fees paid (zero, or reimbursed). On arrival there is a passport-custody check, then monthly wage-receipt confirmations. Short translated voice check-ins provide independent verification. The worker holds the credential and shares it on consent with employers and brands, which see aggregate dashboards. Over time it accrues employment history and endorsements usable for the next placement or a remittance-backed loan.
why_now: Law firms published compliance roadmaps for the regulation in September 2026, and brands are starting to build supplier evidence programs 15 months before enforcement. Recruitment-fee evidence is the hardest part to get, and no one holds it continuously.
revenue_model: $10-25 per hire paid by the employer or brand, per-site dashboard subscriptions, and placement referral fees from ethical recruiters later.
non_obvious_insight: Compliance buyers must prove a negative, and only worker-side records can do that. Audits fail because they sample, while a worker-held receipt makes evidence continuous, cheaper and self-enforcing. Because the same credential improves the worker's mobility, the worker's incentives align with the buyer's.
first_30_days: Partner with two ethical recruiters in one corridor and one EU-facing supplier. Pilot for 200 hires using a WhatsApp bot rather than an app. Charge a $5k pilot fee plus a per-hire fee, and write up the evidence pack in the format a brand's compliance team will accept.
